# Fact-base file format (src/<id>.md)

This file is the ONLY fact base lesson authors may use. An automatic check rejects any number or
quotation in a lesson that does not appear in this file. So: put every usable fact here, verbatim where
possible, and nothing that is not verified.

```
**Chapter N**

<Title, short, plain>

*<Framing question, exactly as given to you>*

<Narrative, 350 to 700 words, plain short sentences, past tense, no em dashes.
 Tell the case in order, with real dates, times, counts, money, names of roles (and names of public
 officials or executives only where the record names them). Put exact short quotations from the
 primary record in typographic quotes “like this”, with who said or wrote it. Every number you will
 want a lesson to show must appear here as digits (e.g. 9,483 and 9483 both fine; write "about 45
 minutes" exactly as the source does).>

THE RECORD

<Bullet list of the real documents/objects in the record (the order, the report, the email, the
 alert, the log), each with the fields the source gives: dates, ids, counts, sender, subject, exact
 wording if known. Say "not published" where the object exists but its text is not public.>

THE CHAIN

<Numbered list of 4 to 7 actors/decisions in order. For each: the role, what they did, and whether
 the source says a control (check, verify, revoke, block) could have broken the chain there. Mark those
 links CONTROL POINT, and give the source's own words for why.>

WHAT THE RECORD RECOMMENDS

<The regulator's / review board's / company's own recommendations or lessons, quoted where possible.
 This becomes the lesson's takeaway, so include one or two concrete things a practitioner can do.>

CAUTIONS

<Facts that are disputed, secondary-only, sensitive or easy to over-claim. Lesson authors must obey these.>

ELSEWHERE

<2 or 3 one-line related incidents with month/year, each with a URL listed in NOTES. Only if verified.>

---
NOTES
1 <Source title, publisher, date>. <URL>
2 ...
```

Rules
- Primary sources first. Mark secondary-sourced facts "(reported by X)".
- No invention. If unsure, leave it out or put it under CAUTIONS.
- No em dashes anywhere. Use commas or full stops.
- Keep sensitive data out (no names of junior staff, no personal data from leaks).
